items.title: Louis Gallaud Interview, 1960-03-18
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Red' at the end of a list of musicians ('Cornette player... And then the trombone player... Red.') and the interviewer clarifies 'Red Clark'. The interviewee does not describe a personal interaction, collaboration, or relationship with Red Clark, only listing him in the con

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Me and him and Jim Crow. Yeah, that's right. I saw you then. I remember. Because he didn't play in our scene, you know. He was in the band. Sure, I remember now seeing you. I forgot about that. Yeah, in the band. I was talking to Pryju too. I worked with Pryju too. A couple times. You know Willie Pryju. Yes. Cornette player. Yeah. A couple times. And then the trombone player. He used to play trombone and now he plays the bass on. Red.
Red Clark, yeah. Mm-hmm. How did Pryju rank in the old days? Was he considered one of the best ones?

Oh yeah, he was, he had a, say, a cranny like a pipe. Yeah, he still has a little. He had that cranny like a pipe. Yeah, he used to play that drum. Yeah, he used to play. He could play too. Yeah. And him and Louis was good friends. They used to play each other, help each other out around, around Pete Lyle was around there when he was playing there with Marie and Arthur and Benville. Marie and Ben, I was there. I was there. I was there with Marie. I think it is. Over there with Benville.
